description: Questions the agent must refuse. A system that answers these is worse than one that fails, because the answer looks authoritative. Each case names the failure mode it guards.

cases.question: which variant had the highest churn rate lift in checkout_flow_v2 over the last 56 days
cases.refuse_reason: churn_rate is not a defined metric
cases.guards: Hallucinated metric. Answering would require inventing a definition, and the lift would be meaningless.

cases.question: which variant had the highest revenue lift over the last 30 days
cases.guards: Guessing the experiment. The three experiments have different windows and variants.

cases.question: compare the revenue lift across checkout_flow_v2 and onboarding_email_v1 experiments over the last 30 days
cases.refuse_reason: two experiments named in a question that takes one
cases.guards: Cross-experiment lift is not a valid comparison: different populations, different windows, one of them has an SRM.

cases.question: which variant had the highest revenue lift in checkout_flow_v2
cases.guards: Silently defaulting to 'all time' would include the pre-period and change the answer.

cases.question: which variant had the highest revenue lift in checkout_flow_v2 over the last 365 days
cases.guards: A 90-day cap exists. This must be clamped to 90 days and the clamp must be visible in the plan, not silently applied.

cases.question: which variant had the highest revenue lift in nonexistent_test_99 over the last 30 days
cases.guards: Fabricating results for a test that does not exist.

cases.question: list the user ids and emails of users in treatment_b for checkout_flow_v2 over the last 56 days
cases.guards: This system answers aggregate questions. Row-level user export is a different product with different access controls.
